#This dataset tests if the presence of bird species on given islands is affected by the area of the island or the isolation of the islands (how far each is from the mainland). The predictor (independent) variables are "area" and "isolation" while the response (dependent) variable is "incidence." 

#All variables:
incidence (dependent)
area (independent)
isolation (independent)

#Modeling just the intercept:
> mod_intercept <- lm(Isolation$incidence~1)

#Modeling combinations of the two predictors:
> mod1 <- lm(Isolation$incidence~Isolation$area, data = Isolation)
> mod2 <- lm(Isolation$incidence~Isolation$isolation, data = Isolation)
> mod3 <- lm(Isolation$incidence~Isolation$area*Isolation$isolation, data = Isolation)
> mod4 <- lm(Isolation$incidence~Isolation$area+Isolation$isolation, data = Isolation)

#First load the package AICcmodavg
> library(AICcmodavg)

#AICc:
> AICc(mod_intercept)
[1] 75.53779

> AICc(mod1)
[1] 59.49274

> AICc(mod2)
[1] 45.55016

> AICc(mod3)      #This has the lowest AICc!
[1] 38.92573

> AICc(mod4)
[1] 39.21524

#Calculate delta AICC:
#Delta AICC is calculated as the difference between the current model and the AICc model with the minimum value.
> AICc(mod_intercept) - AICc(mod3)
[1] 36.61206

> AICc(mod1) - AICc(mod3)
[1] 20.56701

> AICc(mod2) - AICc(mod3)
[1] 6.624427

> AICc(mod3) - AICc(mod3)
[1] 0

> AICc(mod4) - AICc(mod3)
[1] 0.2895125

#mod3 <- lm(Isolation$incidence~Isolation$area*Isolation$isolation, data = Isolation)
#Checks the correlation of the incidence (dependent) to the multiplication of the area (independent) and the isolation (independent)

#From summary(mod3), isolation on its own is significant, however area and the interaction of the two predictors -- area and isolation -- are not significant.

#From summary(mod4), area on its own and isolation on its own are each significant.

#Simple scatter plots (result in the exact same graphs):
> plot(incidence~area*isolation, data = Isolation, pch = 16)
> plot(incidence~area+isolation, data = Isolation, pch = 16)

#The best model is mod3 <- lm(Isolation$incidence~Isolation$area*Isolation$isolation, data = Isolation), followed by mod4 <- lm(Isolation$incidence~Isolation$area+Isolation$isolation, data = Isolation). These two models have the lowest values as an AICc and when calculated as a delta AICC.

#From my analysis, I have determined that both "area" and "isolation" can be significant when determining the presence of bird species on an island in this dataset. Which predictor variable, or both, are significant depends on the model run.
